display.title: Rosh Chodesh: Why the First Day Is the Head of the Month
display.summary_short: On the eve of Rosh Chodesh Av, Uncle Yossi explains why the first of the month is called its 'head' and why our conduct that day matters so much.
display.summary_long: A short holiday talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show, given on the night of Rosh Chodesh Av. Uncle Yossi points out that 'Rosh' does not mean new but head: Rosh Chodesh is the head of the whole month. Just as the head guides the entire body and every limb draws its life from it, every day of the Jewish month is linked to its first day. On Rosh Chodesh the heavenly blessings for health, life and sustenance, food, clothing and shelter, are granted and then shared out over the rest of the month. That is why we say special prayers on Rosh Chodesh, and why our behavior that day is so important, as we pass before Hashem, our merciful King, for a good and blessed judgment.
display.lesson: Make Rosh Chodesh special, because it sets the blessings for the whole month.
